facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Recurring post sale revenue gives the business cash visibility, but the installed base is shrinking and the 2026 recovery is cost-led. Post sale revenue was 79% of FY2025 revenue and equipment sales 21%, management says the business does not depend on a single customer or a few customers, and about 43% of revenue is earned outside the United States. Committed multi-year service obligations were USD 636 million at 2026-09-30 against USD 644 million at 2025-12-31, which is small beside post sale revenue because most service revenue is invoiced as rendered. On a pro forma basis that treats the acquired businesses as owned throughout, revenue fell 7.6% in 2025 and 5.0% in the first nine months of 2026, while adjusted operating income rose to USD 399 million from USD 243 million, which the issuer attributes to integration synergies and cost discipline. A licensing agreement added 1.1 percentage points to third quarter 2026 revenue, so the decline before it was 5.8% rather than 4.7%. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Growth has been bought with secured and high-coupon debt, so the two acquisitions add to creditor risk until the synergies are proven. ITsavvy cost USD 404 million in November 2024, of which USD 210 million was seller notes at fair value. Lexmark cost USD 768 million for the equity at closing in July 2025, against a headline of USD 1.5 billion that included net debt and other assumed liabilities, and USD 749 million after the working capital adjustment, and was financed alongside USD 500 million of 13.5% second lien notes and USD 250 million of 13.00% senior notes due 2030 whose coupon steps up to 16.75% by July 2030, while USD 327 million of incremental first lien term loans refinanced USD 323 million of Lexmark's own debt. Lexmark contributed USD 962 million of 2025 revenue, 13.70% of the total, and a net loss of USD 119 million. The synergy target has risen from more than USD 200 million within two years to more than USD 300 million by the end of 2027. In September 2023 the company bought about USD 542 million of its shares from Carl C. Icahn and affiliates at USD 15.84 per share, funded by a USD 555 million loan that was refinanced with the USD 550 million Term Loan B. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The Xerox brand and related intellectual property now sit in a joint venture financed ahead of the other creditors, which is the largest change to the structure since the acquisitions. In February 2026 funds managed by Angelo, Gordon & Co. (together called TPG) and other investors lent USD 405 million of five-year senior secured term loans and bought USD 45 million of Class A units of XRX Brandco Holdings LLC, about USD 450 million in all, with the term loans secured on substantially all assets of the entity and its subsidiary, including the contributed intellectual property. Xerox Corporation consolidates the entity, and the royalty of 2.0% of specified revenue that the licensees pay it is held in a reserve account for the lenders, with certain subsidiaries of Holdings guaranteeing and securing the licence obligations. The joint venture can end the licence on certain defaults by Holdings, including insolvency or a change of control, after which the licensees keep only a 90-day sell-off period for inventory, so a default would put the use of the brand itself at stake. The term loans cost more than 11% a year even at the reference rate floor and the instruments amortize USD 81 million a year from the fourth quarter of 2026, and 10.37% of principal debt now sits in subsidiaries below Xerox Corporation, almost all of it in this joint venture. Whether the contributed assets had been collateral for the existing first and second lien notes is not established. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–13, 39, 99, 101; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 262–263; calculation C8; calculation C9; calculation C10; calculation C11

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Ownership and control are not established, so shareholder willingness cannot be assessed and the medium governance risk rests on issuer behaviour alone. The annual report places beneficial ownership, directors, compensation and related-party items in a proxy statement that is not supplied, no controlling holder or financial sponsor is named, and the holder of the Series A preferred stock is not named. Four of the six executive officers took their present roles in 2025, including a chief financial officer who joined with Lexmark. Reporting is audited with effective internal control, but Lexmark was left out of the 2025 internal control audit, representing 13% of assets and 14% of revenue, and its purchase accounting needed corrections in both the fourth quarter of 2025 and the second quarter of 2026. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Liability management is selective across note series and holders, which raises class-specific risk for unsecured noteholders. In 2026 the company repurchased USD 194 million of its 5.50% notes due 2028 and USD 6 million of its 13.5% second lien notes due 2031 for about USD 101 million, 50.50% of principal, and booked a USD 95 million gain over nine months. In October 2026 it agreed with certain holders to exchange about USD 174 million of the 2028 notes for about USD 120 million of new 10.25% first lien notes of Xerox Corporation and shares equal to 2.93% of those outstanding, cutting principal by up to about USD 54 million and moving USD 120 million of maturities from 2028 to 2030. The exchanged claims would rank ahead of the roughly USD 382 million of 2028 notes left outstanding, and no supplied document confirms that the exchange closed. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a cautious reading is operating and liquidity. Adjusted operating income was USD 399 million in the first nine months of 2026 against USD 243 million on a pro forma basis a year earlier, the adjusted operating margin of 6.6% in the third quarter was 3.3 percentage points higher than a year before, and management states that cash on hand, cash from operations and ABL availability cover at least twelve months of needs without capital markets. The debt-funded buyback is three years old, dividends are being cut and suspended, 2026 repurchases were made at about half of par, and the joint venture raised USD 404 million of net proceeds without issuing common equity. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Xerox presents a weak business profile supported by a recurring revenue base, a cost programme and liquidity to the end of 2027, but credit quality is constrained by high leverage, thin interest cover, weak cash generation and negative equity. Cash-flow durability appears weak because operating cash flow turned negative and guidance was cut. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on delivery of the cost programme, receivable sales and the willingness of lenders to accept more secured debt. The primary downside path is falling operating cash flow ahead of the 2028 and 2029 maturities. Further analysis would require an issuer-stated EBITDA, interim cash interest, ratings and prices and the executed debt documents. Top risk: refinancing the 2028 and 2029 maturities on falling operating cash flow. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 95–97; calculation C1; calculation C5

## Request

Source readiness for Xerox Holdings Corp (issuer xrx-1770450), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway for the requested financial foundation, business and governance, and fundamental credit work. The scope is whether the five supplied filings can support that work and what is missing.
## Sources

| 10-Q_2026-03-31_xrx-20260331.htm.jsonl | Combined quarterly report on Form 10-Q of Xerox Holdings Corporation and Xerox Corporation for the quarter ended March 31, 2026 | 2026-05-07 | f7db690229ad2f37021ede5f6c82f0e77ea2811a1d390fe25917b83e63aea88f | Q1 2026 statements, joint venture financing and exhibit index |

## Findings
### Bottom line

The five supplied filings support the requested credit snapshot of Xerox Holdings Corporation to 30 September 2026 from primary evidence, but covenant, priority, rating and pricing views cannot be drawn from them, so a creditor should treat those as open. The set is two annual reports and three quarterly reports of the combined filing with Xerox Corporation, and the latest was signed 13 days before the as-of date.

Three limits matter. An exchange of 2028 senior notes was expected to close on or about 2026-11-13, 5 days before the as-of date, and nothing supplied confirms it closed. The executed indentures and credit agreements are not supplied, so covenant and security terms rest on the filings' own summaries. The quarterly reports print neither cash interest paid nor EBITDA, so trailing interest coverage can only be derived from statement lines and must be labelled as derived.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Reported EBITDA is negative for the twelve months to 30 September 2026 after a goodwill impairment, and net debt is 4.46x house-adjusted EBITDA, so creditors rely on cash flow that was negative for nine months. House-adjusted EBITDA of USD 854 million is the issuer's adjusted operating income plus depreciation and equipment financing interest, an analyst measure, because the issuer states no EBITDA.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3–6, 21, 24; calculation C55; calculation C56; calculation C58

Cash of USD 412 million and net ABL availability of about USD 225 million exceed the USD 217 million of principal due to the end of 2027, but USD 752 million falls due in 2028 and needs refinancing. Management expects full-year operating cash flow of USD 145 million to USD 195 million, which needs USD 222 million to USD 272 million in the fourth quarter, and an exchange of 2028 notes expected to close on 2026-11-13 is not confirmed.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 42, 56, 95, 97, 100–101; calculation C41; calculation C39; calculation C40

### Leverage and coverage

The issuer states no EBITDA, so the reported measure is derived from the statements and it absorbs the third-quarter 2026 goodwill impairment of USD 959 million, which leaves EBITDA for the twelve months to 30 September 2026 at negative USD 275 million and total debt over EBITDA not calculable, as it is for FY2024, when a USD 1,058 million impairment had the same effect. At FY2025, with no impairment, reported EBITDA of USD 177 million gives total debt of 23.99x and cover of 0.65x on the USD 272 million of cash interest paid, which shows how little earnings stood behind the debt before Lexmark contributed for a full year.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 150, 152, 227; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; calculation C55; calculation C64

On the house-adjusted measure, net debt is 4.46x LTM EBITDA against 6.42x at FY2025 and 4.64x at FY2024, and total debt is 4.94x against 7.30x at FY2025. The improvement is earnings, not repayment: net debt rose by USD 73 million from 2025-12-31 to 2026-09-30, while adjusted operating income for the nine months was USD 399 million against USD 146 million a year earlier, a rise of USD 253 million, which the issuer attributes to integration synergies and cost discipline, although revenue fell 4.7% in the third quarter of 2026 against a third quarter 2025 that already included Lexmark, so the gain is cost-led.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 151, 187; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 21, 59, 66; calculation C58; calculation C60; calculation C62; calculation C59; calculation C61; calculation C65; calculation C67

The house measure is generous in two ways. It excludes restructuring charges and the non-service cost of retirement plans, although the company paid USD 60 million for restructuring and contributed USD 118 million to retirement plans in the first nine months of 2026, and it adds back equipment financing interest so that it matches total debt that includes USD 1,296 million of financing debt supporting finance receivables and operating lease equipment. Against core debt of USD 2,924 million, the ratio to adjusted operating income plus depreciation is 3.75x, against 5.56x at FY2025, whose earnings held Lexmark for only six months.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 123, 187; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 24, 100; calculation C63

The strongest evidence against a cautious view is the recovery in adjusted operating income and the issuer's own targets: it states run-rate synergies above USD 300 million by the end of 2027, and the October 2026 exchange would cut principal by up to about USD 54 million while moving about USD 120 million of maturities from 2028 to 2030. That view would win if operating cash flow converts: management's range for 2026 needs USD 222 million to USD 272 million in the fourth quarter, against USD 208 million in the fourth quarter of 2025, and a shortfall would leave interest, restructuring and the 2028 maturities to be funded from cash and the ABL.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 152; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 56, 97; calculation C38; calculation C39; calculation C40
### Cash flow quality

Operating cash flow was negative USD 77 million in the first nine months of 2026 against positive USD 16 million a year earlier, and free cash flow after USD 70 million of capital expenditure was negative USD 147 million. Operating cash flow includes USD 152 million from the run-off of finance receivables, down from USD 338 million, and the issuer attributes weaker liquidity in 2026 to lower profitability and lower proceeds from sales of finance receivables; without the run-off, operating cash flow was negative USD 229 million against negative USD 322 million.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6, 95; calculation C35; calculation C44; calculation C45

Dividends paid fell to USD 24 million from USD 65 million, and the board suspended common and preferred dividend payments from January 2027, which the issuer expects to conserve about USD 28 million a year. The issuer also sold rights to USD 105 million of tariff refund receivables for about USD 80 million of cash, shown in financing activities, and carries a related financing liability of USD 81 million outside total debt, while its supplier finance program, at USD 12 million against accounts payable of USD 1,484 million, is not a material funding float.
### Liquidity and refinancing

Cash and cash equivalents were USD 412 million at 2026-09-30, with restricted cash of USD 118 million held separately, and net ABL availability was about USD 225 million after USD 75 million of borrowings and about USD 66 million of letters of credit, together USD 637 million. Principal due is USD 20 million in the fourth quarter of 2026 and USD 197 million in 2027, then USD 752 million in 2028, USD 1,137 million in 2029 and USD 1,042 million in 2030, so USD 2,931 million falls due in the three years from 2028, including the ABL in May 2028 and the term loan in November 2029.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 37, 42, 95, 100–101; calculation C43; calculation C66

The joint venture financing adds scheduled amortization of about USD 81 million a year from the fourth quarter of 2026. Management states that liquidity is sufficient for at least twelve months from 2026-11-05 without relying on capital markets, but expects to address the 2028 and 2029 maturities through cash from operations, refinancings and exchanges whose timing and terms are uncertain.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 39, 95; calculation C42
### Data quality, definitions and subsequent events

Debt is measured at balance-sheet carrying value of USD 4,220 million, which is USD 128 million below the USD 4,348 million of principal because of USD 95 million of issuance costs and USD 33 million of net discount; the tariff financing liability of USD 81 million is outside this figure, while the joint venture term loans and Class A Units of about USD 450 million are inside it.

Dashes in the statements are carried as not supplied, not as zero, which affects the goodwill impairment, divestitures, short-term debt and tariff liability lines. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 6, 7; calculation C54

## Gaps

Cash paid for interest is not printed in the three 2026 quarterly reports, so cover on cash interest cannot be built for the first quarter, the first half, the nine months or any twelve-month period to 2026, and only FY2024 (USD 214 million) and FY2025 (USD 272 million) are available. This restricts every coverage conclusion after FY2025. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain interim cash flow supplements or earnings releases that state interest paid.

The issuer states no EBITDA or adjusted EBITDA, so reported EBITDA is derived and includes the USD 959 million goodwill impairment and the USD 1,058 million impairment of FY2024. Total debt and net debt over EBITDA are not calculable for FY2024 and the twelve months to 2026-09-30, no EBITDA bridge can be drawn, and the house-adjusted measure used instead is an analyst judgement. Severity: Low, because both measures are shown and labelled. Action: obtain the issuer's own adjusted EBITDA definition.

No instrument-level debt table is printed after 2025-12-31, so the instrument register and the debt stack are drawn at that date and do not show the 2026 repurchases, the joint venture financing, the ABL borrowing or the exchange. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the current debt schedule.

The debt exchange expected to close on 2026-11-13 is not confirmed by any supplied document, so debt after the balance sheet date is stated only as expected. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the later report of the closing and its final terms.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 56

ABL availability is stated at filing dates on a month-end calculation, not at balance-sheet dates, and is not stated for the FY2024 and FY2025 year ends, so undrawn facilities are not supplied for those two dates. Severity: Low. Action: obtain borrowing base certificates.

The issuer does not split cash, operating cash flow, capital expenditure or free cash flow between its finance receivables business and the rest, and splits only debt into financing debt and core debt on an assumed 7 to 1 ratio of debt to equity, so industrial leverage is shown on debt and earnings only. Severity: Low. Action: obtain any segment cash flow disclosure.

Cash flow statements are year to date, discrete cash flows for the second and third quarters of 2026 and the fourth quarter of 2025 are not printed and are not derived here, except the fourth quarter 2025 operating cash flow taken once as the full year less nine months for the comparison with management's range, dashes in the statements are carried as not supplied, and balance sheets at the 2025 interim dates are not supplied. Severity: Low. Action: none needed for the requested snapshot.

spans.text: # Business & governance for Xerox Holdings Corp (xrx-1770450), as of 2026-11-18
## Request

Business and governance for Xerox Holdings Corp (issuer xrx-1770450), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the issuer's business, ownership and corporate structure, transactions and new debt, and governance and shareholder behaviour, drawn from the five supplied filings. The source readiness findings set the limits of what the filings can support.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2024-12-31_xrx-20241231.htm.jsonl | Combined annual report on Form 10-K of Xerox Holdings Corporation and Xerox Corporation for the year ended December 31, 2024 | 2025-02-24 | 7feadaeacdba2056351f3b6fa451718d0a975d778f8ada2b07315b3202b0d082 | Business strategy and the pending Lexmark acquisition as described in early 2025, the March 2024 note issues and the 2023 share repurchase cash flows |

| 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl | Combined annual report on Form 10-K of Xerox Holdings Corporation and Xerox Corporation for the year ended December 31, 2025 | 2026-03-16 | 9a3f813d924828f1b7d797af8da7a5ef15cd20354158f2cb606ad04ab04e3b1f | Business description, segments, geography, acquisitions, notes issued in 2025, preferred stock, share repurchase and warrant notes, executive officers and subsequent events |

| 10-Q_2026-03-31_xrx-20260331.htm.jsonl | Combined quarterly report on Form 10-Q of Xerox Holdings Corporation and Xerox Corporation for the quarter ended March 31, 2026 | 2026-05-07 | f7db690229ad2f37021ede5f6c82f0e77ea2811a1d390fe25917b83e63aea88f | First quarter 2026 note repurchases and the first report carrying the joint venture financing |

| 10-Q_2026-06-30_xrx-20260630.htm.jsonl | Combined quarterly report on Form 10-Q of Xerox Holdings Corporation and Xerox Corporation for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 | 2026-08-06 | 52663691e8f3ced2f8a35e6e1576f98f8f351b2b15809429d3f39554e0a1453c | Second quarter 2026 note repurchases, the third ABL amendment and the exhibit index |

| 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl | Combined quarterly report on Form 10-Q of Xerox Holdings Corporation and Xerox Corporation for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 | 2026-11-05 | 0bee43d9f1f3367610dc24e2dc5d0026067b8b84f672c416d585d1e27999a0b4 | Latest segment results, joint venture terms, goodwill impairment, equity, debt by obligor, subsequent events and cover share count |
| Handoff module | sha256 | Use |

| Source readiness (CP-0) | f5386ee8f2391c8fb25377fd1a74c87f13676ae084fda194ba544da60b4b2843 | Source limits: no executed legal documents, no ratings or market data, the debt exchange not confirmed, the proxy statement not supplied |
## Findings
### Bottom line

Creditors rely on a shrinking print business with no identified controlling shareholder, two debt-funded acquisitions, negative book equity and a brand now held in a joint venture whose lenders have first call on it, so structure and priority matter most.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 84; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–12; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 190–194; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 269, 271; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C8; calculation C16

Management's capital allocation has moved toward creditors: common dividends declared fell 81.51% from 2023 to 2025 and are suspended from January 2027, and 2026 repurchases retired about USD 200 million of notes for about USD 101 million. The 2023 buyback of about USD 542 million of shares from one holder group was debt-funded, ownership is not established, and governance risk is medium.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 126, 254; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 40, 56; calculation C12; calculation C14; calculation C7
### Key findings

Recurring post sale revenue gives the business cash visibility, but the installed base is shrinking and the 2026 recovery is cost-led. Post sale revenue was 79% of FY2025 revenue and equipment sales 21%, management says the business does not depend on a single customer or a few customers, and about 43% of revenue is earned outside the United States. Committed multi-year service obligations were USD 636 million at 2026-09-30 against USD 644 million at 2025-12-31, which is small beside post sale revenue because most service revenue is invoiced as rendered. On a pro forma basis that treats the acquired businesses as owned throughout, revenue fell 7.6% in 2025 and 5.0% in the first nine months of 2026, while adjusted operating income rose to USD 399 million from USD 243 million, which the issuer attributes to integration synergies and cost discipline. A licensing agreement added 1.1 percentage points to third quarter 2026 revenue, so the decline before it was 5.8% rather than 4.7%.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 84; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 59, 62, 66–67, 112; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 183; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C27; calculation C13; calculation C28

Growth has been bought with secured and high-coupon debt, so the two acquisitions add to creditor risk until the synergies are proven. ITsavvy cost USD 404 million in November 2024, of which USD 210 million was seller notes at fair value. Lexmark cost USD 768 million for the equity at closing in July 2025, against a headline of USD 1.5 billion that included net debt and other assumed liabilities, and USD 749 million after the working capital adjustment, and was financed alongside USD 500 million of 13.5% second lien notes and USD 250 million of 13.00% senior notes due 2030 whose coupon steps up to 16.75% by July 2030, while USD 327 million of incremental first lien term loans refinanced USD 323 million of Lexmark's own debt. Lexmark contributed USD 962 million of 2025 revenue, 13.70% of the total, and a net loss of USD 119 million. The synergy target has risen from more than USD 200 million within two years to more than USD 300 million by the end of 2027.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 190–194, 218–222; 10-K_2024-12-31_xrx-20241231.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8, 183; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C6

Shareholder distributions have been cut hard, which supports creditors, but the preferred stock keeps accruing and the last large distribution was debt-funded. Common dividends declared were USD 146 million in 2023, USD 128 million in 2024 and USD 27 million in 2025, after the annual dividend was cut from USD 1.00 to USD 0.50 per share in the first quarter of 2025 and to USD 0.10 in the second. The suspension from January 2027 is expected to conserve about USD 28 million a year, yet the Series A preferred stock, with a liquidation value of USD 180 million and a cumulative 8% dividend of USD 14 million a year, continues to accumulate dividends during the suspension. In September 2023 the company bought about USD 542 million of its shares from Carl C. Icahn and affiliates at USD 15.84 per share, funded by a USD 555 million loan that was refinanced with the USD 550 million Term Loan B.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 126, 153–154, 222, 252, 254; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 56; calculation C7; calculation C12; calculation C15

The Xerox brand and related intellectual property now sit in a joint venture financed ahead of the other creditors, which is the largest change to the structure since the acquisitions. In February 2026 funds managed by Angelo, Gordon & Co. (together called TPG) and other investors lent USD 405 million of five-year senior secured term loans and bought USD 45 million of Class A units of XRX Brandco Holdings LLC, about USD 450 million in all, with the term loans secured on substantially all assets of the entity and its subsidiary, including the contributed intellectual property. Xerox Corporation consolidates the entity, and the royalty of 2.0% of specified revenue that the licensees pay it is held in a reserve account for the lenders, with certain subsidiaries of Holdings guaranteeing and securing the licence obligations. The joint venture can end the licence on certain defaults by Holdings, including insolvency or a change of control, after which the licensees keep only a 90-day sell-off period for inventory, so a default would put the use of the brand itself at stake. The term loans cost more than 11% a year even at the reference rate floor and the instruments amortize USD 81 million a year from the fourth quarter of 2026, and 10.37% of principal debt now sits in subsidiaries below Xerox Corporation, almost all of it in this joint venture. Whether the contributed assets had been collateral for the existing first and second lien notes is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–13, 39, 99, 101; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 262–263; calculation C8; calculation C9; calculation C10; calculation C11

Book equity has gone, so reported numbers no longer show any loss-absorbing layer beneath the debt. After the USD 959 million goodwill impairment on the Print and Other reporting unit in the third quarter of 2026, Holdings reports a shareholders' deficit of USD 683 million against equity of USD 444 million at 2025-12-31, Xerox Corporation reports a deficit of USD 492 million, and USD 897 million of goodwill remains on that unit. The issuer warns that future impairments may be possible if forecasts weaken further.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 13, 48, 51; calculation C16

Ownership and control are not established, so shareholder willingness cannot be assessed and the medium governance risk rests on issuer behaviour alone. The annual report places beneficial ownership, directors, compensation and related-party items in a proxy statement that is not supplied, no controlling holder or financial sponsor is named, and the holder of the Series A preferred stock is not named. Four of the six executive officers took their present roles in 2025, including a chief financial officer who joined with Lexmark. Reporting is audited with effective internal control, but Lexmark was left out of the 2025 internal control audit, representing 13% of assets and 14% of revenue, and its purchase accounting needed corrections in both the fourth quarter of 2025 and the second quarter of 2026.

Liability management is selective across note series and holders, which raises class-specific risk for unsecured noteholders. In 2026 the company repurchased USD 194 million of its 5.50% notes due 2028 and USD 6 million of its 13.5% second lien notes due 2031 for about USD 101 million, 50.50% of principal, and booked a USD 95 million gain over nine months. In October 2026 it agreed with certain holders to exchange about USD 174 million of the 2028 notes for about USD 120 million of new 10.25% first lien notes of Xerox Corporation and shares equal to 2.93% of those outstanding, cutting principal by up to about USD 54 million and moving USD 120 million of maturities from 2028 to 2030. The exchanged claims would rank ahead of the roughly USD 382 million of 2028 notes left outstanding, and no supplied document confirms that the exchange closed.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 40, 42, 56; 10-Q_2026-03-31_xrx-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 216–217; calculation C14; calculation C18; calculation C19; calculation C20

Cash generation leans on receivable sales and a single supplier, which makes the operating model less self-funding than its recurring revenue suggests. Net cash used in operating activities was USD 77 million in the first nine months of 2026 against USD 16 million provided a year earlier, with proceeds from sales of finance receivables down from USD 1,102 million in 2023 to USD 357 million in 2025 and USD 122 million in the nine months, and sales that meet certain criteria can force early repayment of first lien debt. Purchases from FUJIFILM Business Innovation, the largest strategic sourcing partner, were USD 811 million in 2025, 11.55% of revenue, and management says it has outsourced a material portion of manufacturing to such partners.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 34, 99; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 20, 28, 129, 205; calculation C21; calculation C22
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious reading is operating and liquidity. Adjusted operating income was USD 399 million in the first nine months of 2026 against USD 243 million on a pro forma basis a year earlier, the adjusted operating margin of 6.6% in the third quarter was 3.3 percentage points higher than a year before, and management states that cash on hand, cash from operations and ABL availability cover at least twelve months of needs without capital markets. The debt-funded buyback is three years old, dividends are being cut and suspended, 2026 repurchases were made at about half of par, and the joint venture raised USD 404 million of net proceeds without issuing common equity.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 42, 60, 95, 112; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; calculation C8; calculation C14; calculation C27

The view would turn better if the October 2026 exchange closes on the stated terms, repurchases below par continue, the next annual report names the large holders and an independent board, and the joint venture documents show that existing lenders' collateral did not include the contributed assets. It would turn worse with another transfer of assets into a financing vehicle, more secured debt ahead of the unsecured notes, further purchase accounting corrections, a repeat goodwill impairment, or operating cash flow below the management range of USD 145 million to USD 195 million for 2026, which needs USD 222 million to USD 272 million in the fourth quarter.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 56, 97; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 57; calculation C31
### Limitations

- Beneficial ownership, board membership and related-party disclosures sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied, so the ownership read and the medium governance risk rating cannot be tested against who controls the vote and could move either way if a controlling holder emerges.

- The executed joint venture credit agreement, the licence agreement, the indentures and the intercreditor agreements are not supplied, so the conclusion that the brand is financed ahead of other creditors rests on the filings' own summaries and cannot say whether the contributed assets were previously collateral or what the asset coverage covenant requires.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12, 39; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 219, 222

- No document after 2026-11-05 is supplied, so the exchange that was expected to close on or about 2026-11-13 is described as expected and the class-specific risk finding may be overstated or understated depending on the final terms and participation.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 56

- The quarterly reports now show IT Solutions as its own revenue line while the 2025 annual report split revenue only into equipment sales and post sale revenue, and 2024 revenue lines were recast in that report, so the revenue mix trend mixes two presentations and the shrinking installed base conclusion is stronger on the pro forma growth rates than on the mix shares.

- Customer concentration beyond management's statement, renewal rates for managed print services, and the terms of the product supply agreements with FUJIFILM Business Innovation are not disclosed, and the committed obligations disclosed cover only contracts that are not invoiced as rendered, so revenue visibility and supplier dependence are stated qualitatively and the operating model read could be better or worse.
### Company and operating model
| Dimension | What the filings show | Why it matters to a creditor | Source |

| Business | Management describes Xerox as a workplace technology company building services-led, software-enabled workplace solutions. Print and Other designs, develops and sells document systems, supplies, services and related financing; IT Solutions sells integrated IT infrastructure, managed IT, network, security and cloud services | Cash comes from equipment placements, recurring supplies and service, financing income and IT resale, which differ in margin and cyclicality | 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 8–12 |

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

Two acquisitions explain most of the change in the structure since 2024. ITsavvy, bought on 2024-11-20, created the IT Solutions segment for USD 404 million, of which USD 194 million was cash and USD 210 million was seller notes due in October 2025 and January 2026. Lexmark, bought from Ninestar Group Company Limited on 2025-07-01, cost USD 768 million at closing including USD 93 million of cash acquired, and USD 749 million after a USD 19 million working capital adjustment finalized in the first quarter of 2026. The 2024 annual report described the pending Lexmark deal as USD 1.5 billion inclusive of net debt and other assumed liabilities, and the bridge from that figure to the equity price is not itemised.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 190–194; 10-K_2024-12-31_xrx-20241231.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 183; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; calculation C3; calculation C4

New debt followed the same path. In March 2024 Holdings issued USD 500 million of notes due 2029 and USD 400 million of 3.75% convertible notes due 2030. In April and May 2025 Xerox Corporation issued USD 400 million of 10.25% first lien notes due 2030 at 99% of par and USD 500 million of 13.5% second lien notes due 2031 at 98% and 95% of par, and about USD 494 million of escrowed second lien proceeds was released at the Lexmark closing. On 2025-07-01 Holdings issued USD 125 million of 13.00% unsecured notes due June 2026 and USD 250 million of 13.00% notes due 2030 with a pre-funded warrant, and Xerox Corporation borrowed USD 327 million of incremental first lien term loans. In 2025 Xerox received about USD 375 million from issuing senior notes and about USD 904 million from secured debt.

The February 2026 joint venture is the largest new financing since the 2025 annual report. Xerox Corporation contributed the Xerox brand trademarks and related intellectual property to XRX Brandco Holdings LLC for Class B units, and investors funded USD 405 million of five-year senior secured term loans and USD 45 million of Class A units, which carry a mandatory cumulative redemption in five years unless the holders defer it. The proceeds were distributed to Xerox Corporation for general corporate purposes and for opportunistic work on the capital structure, including debt repayment. The 2025 annual report states USD 42 million of fees, while the third quarter report states USD 46 million paid at closing and USD 8 million later.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 262–263; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–12, 39; calculation C8

Equity-linked and liability management steps followed in 2026. Holders of common stock, Series A preferred stock and the convertible notes received warrants to buy shares at USD 8.00 each for cash or with designated notes, over a number of shares equal to 58.01% of those outstanding, and 1.36% of the warrants had been exercised by 2026-09-30, one exercise retiring about USD 8 million of the convertible notes. The company also repurchased USD 194 million of the 2028 notes and USD 6 million of the 2031 second lien notes, and sold rights to USD 105 million of tariff refund receivables for about USD 80 million of cash, a discount of USD 25 million, which is shown in financing activities with a USD 81 million liability outside total debt at 2026-09-30.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 261; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 40–41, 49; calculation C23; calculation C24; calculation C14; calculation C29

Two announced steps are not yet complete. An exchange of about USD 174 million of 2028 notes for about USD 120 million of new first lien notes of Xerox Corporation and shares equal to 2.93% of those outstanding was expected to close on or about 2026-11-13, and the board suspended common and preferred dividends from January 2027, with the preferred dividend continuing to accumulate. No supplied document confirms the exchange closed.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 56; calculation C18; calculation C19

## Gaps

The proxy statement that holds beneficial ownership, board membership, executive compensation and related-party items is not supplied, so who controls the vote, whether the Icahn parties still hold shares and whether insider arrangements exist cannot be established. This limits the ownership picture and the governance risk level to issuer behaviour. Severity: Material. Action: obtain the 2026 proxy statement.

The executed joint venture credit agreement, the licence agreement and guarantee, the indentures and the intercreditor agreements are not supplied, so whether the contributed brand assets were collateral for earlier notes, and how much room remains for further secured debt, cannot be tested. Severity: Material. Action: obtain the agreements.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12, 39; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 219, 222

The levels of the asset coverage ratio and the minimum revenue covenants in the joint venture documents are not stated, so headroom against a default or a call for extra support from Xerox cannot be measured. Severity: Material. Action: obtain the joint venture agreements and any compliance certificates.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12

No document after 2026-11-05 is supplied, so the closing and final terms of the 2028 notes exchange, the participants in it and whether it was open to all holders are not established. Severity: Minor. Action: obtain the next quarterly report or a current report on the closing.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 56

The terms of Amendment No. 2 to the first lien term loan agreement, filed by reference to a current report dated 2026-10-29, are not stated in the supplied reports, so any change to baskets or covenants ahead of the exchange is not established. Severity: Minor. Action: obtain the amendment.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 114

Customer concentration beyond management's statement, renewal rates for managed print services and the terms of the supply agreements with FUJIFILM Business Innovation are not disclosed, so revenue visibility and supplier dependence are stated qualitatively. Severity: Minor. Action: obtain management disclosure and the supply agreements.

The holder of the Series A preferred stock, the notes designated for warrant exercise and the rating agency and rating level are not named in the supplied filings, so the vote held by the preferred stock, the route for exchanging debt for equity and rating-linked terms cannot be assessed. Severity: Minor. Action: obtain the proxy statement, the warrant agreement and rating reports.

The filings state different figures for the ITsavvy price, the Lexmark headline and equity price, the joint venture fees, the issuer of the 13.00% notes due 2030 and the synergy target; each is shown in the conflict log with its sources and none is reconciled beyond the choice stated there. Severity: Minor. Action: none needed for this snapshot unless the Lexmark headline size matters, in which case obtain the purchase agreement.

spans.text: # Fundamental credit for Xerox Holdings Corp (xrx-1770450), as of 2026-11-18
## Request

Fundamental credit for Xerox Holdings Corp (issuer xrx-1770450), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the overall fundamental credit profile of the issuer, its strongest support, its weakest dimension and its primary downside path, drawn from the five supplied filings and the earlier module findings. Security selection, legal capacity, recovery and portfolio sizing are outside this scope.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2024-12-31_xrx-20241231.htm.jsonl | Combined annual report on Form 10-K of Xerox Holdings Corporation and Xerox Corporation for the year ended December 31, 2024 | 2025-02-24 | 7feadaeacdba2056351f3b6fa451718d0a975d778f8ada2b07315b3202b0d082 | Strategy and the pending Lexmark deal as described in early 2025; the 2023 repurchase and 2024 notes |

| 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl | Combined annual report on Form 10-K of Xerox Holdings Corporation and Xerox Corporation for the year ended December 31, 2025 | 2026-03-16 | 9a3f813d924828f1b7d797af8da7a5ef15cd20354158f2cb606ad04ab04e3b1f | FY2025 business, segment, interest, debt, equity and subsequent-event notes; cost and supply risk factors |

| 10-Q_2026-03-31_xrx-20260331.htm.jsonl | Combined quarterly report on Form 10-Q of Xerox Holdings Corporation and Xerox Corporation for the quarter ended March 31, 2026 | 2026-05-07 | f7db690229ad2f37021ede5f6c82f0e77ea2811a1d390fe25917b83e63aea88f | First quarter 2026 repurchases and the first statements carrying the joint venture financing |

| Handoff module | sha256 | Use |
| Source readiness (CP-0) | f5386ee8f2391c8fb25377fd1a74c87f13676ae084fda194ba544da60b4b2843 | Source limits: no ratings or prices, no executed documents, exchange unconfirmed |
| Financial foundation (CP-1) | a4e1a3e91a40f325cd7ea8069443db81959073c5c4b6e99cab302c18b4abc952 | Statements, EBITDA measures, net debt, leverage, cash flow, liquidity and maturity ladder |
| Business & governance (CP-1A) | 234ca468c95675c146804f1532b0b36093939e3b599f84efdd1cbec8218e2c36 | Business, ownership, structure, transactions and governance behaviour |
## Findings
### Bottom line

Xerox is a weak credit: a shrinking print business carrying total debt of USD 4,220 million with negative reported EBITDA, negative book equity and USD 1,889 million due in 2028 and 2029, so creditors rely on cost savings, receivable sales and refinancing access.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5, 100–101; calculation C1

Liquidity covers the next twelve months on management's account and adjusted earnings are recovering, so a default before 2028 is not the central risk. The central risk is a further fall in operating cash flow that leaves the 2028 and 2029 maturities to be refinanced at coupons above 10%, with a growing share of debt secured ahead of the unsecured notes. Governance risk is medium.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 95, 97; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 218–219; calculation C18; calculation C9
### Key findings

Business risk is weak because a mostly recurring revenue base is shrinking. Post sale revenue was 79% of FY2025 revenue and committed multi-year service obligations were USD 636 million at 2026-09-30, but on a pro forma basis revenue fell 7.6% in 2025 and 5.0% in the first nine months of 2026, and the IT Solutions line fell 12.1%. Equipment installations rose 9.0% in the third quarter of 2026 and the pro forma decline narrowed from the second quarter, which is a first sign of stabilisation rather than a trend.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 84; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 59, 62, 66

Leverage is high and has fallen only because earnings recovered, not because debt fell. Net debt of USD 3,808 million at 2026-09-30 is USD 3,754 million pro forma for the exchange of 2028 notes expected on 2026-11-13, and pro forma net leverage is not established. Net debt is 4.46x house-adjusted EBITDA of USD 854 million for the last twelve months against 6.42x at FY2025, a fall of 1.96x in which net debt rose USD 73 million and EBITDA rose 46.74%. Reported EBITDA is negative USD 275 million for the same twelve months after the USD 959 million goodwill impairment, the issuer states no EBITDA, and its own target of total debt below 3.0x EBITDA compares with 4.94x on the house measure.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C7; calculation C19

Interest absorbs a growing share of earnings, so coverage is thin and falling. Adjusted operating income plus depreciation covered non-financing interest expense 2.18x over the last twelve months against 4.23x in FY2024, because non-financing interest expense rose 64.88% in the first nine months of 2026 and total interest expense rose 41.45%, on higher rates on the Lexmark borrowings and the brand financing, and the 2025 secured issues carry coupons of 10.25% and 13.5%. The 13.00% notes due 2030 step up toward 16.75% by July 2030, and reported EBITDA covered FY2025 cash interest only 0.65x; cash interest is not printed for the 2026 interim periods.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 96, 219–220, 227; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C18; calculation C14

Cash generation is the weakest dimension. Net cash used in operating activities was USD 77 million in the first nine months of 2026, free cash flow for the last twelve months was USD 37 million, or 4.33% of house-adjusted EBITDA against 76.68% in FY2024, and management cut its 2026 operating cash flow guidance to USD 145 million to USD 195 million from about USD 340 million on lower profitability, lower proceeds from sales of finance receivables and lower collections of tariff refunds. The range needs USD 222 million to USD 272 million in the fourth quarter against USD 208 million in the fourth quarter of 2025, and a repeat of last year's quarter would leave the year at USD 131 million, below the range.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 97; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 71; calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C6

Liquidity is adequate to the end of 2027 but the refinancing wall behind it is large. Cash of USD 412 million and net ABL availability of about USD 225 million cover the USD 217 million of principal due to the end of 2027 by 2.94x, and management says liquidity is sufficient for at least twelve months, but principal due is USD 752 million in 2028, USD 1,137 million in 2029 and USD 1,042 million in 2030, USD 2,931 million in all, and the ABL matures in May 2028. Pro forma cash for the exchange is not established, because accrued interest on the exchanged notes is paid in cash and not stated. Management expects to address the maturities through cash from operations, refinancings and liability management whose timing and terms are uncertain.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 42, 56, 95, 100–101; calculation C1; calculation C12

Creditors are increasingly ranked by security and by entity, which raises class-specific risk for unsecured holders. About 47.15% of principal debt is now secured, USD 451 million sits in subsidiaries below Xerox Corporation, USD 450 million of it the brand financing, and the exchange would add about USD 120 million of first lien notes, while management states that further transactions may be pari passu with or effectively senior to existing debt. The company's own estimate puts the fair value of Holdings long-term debt at 49.10% of carrying amount against 76.02% for Xerox Corporation, which is an estimate and not a traded price.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47, 56, 98–99, 101; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 216–217; calculation C9; calculation C8

Financial policy is moving toward creditors but equity no longer protects them, and governance risk is medium. Dividends on common and preferred stock are suspended from January 2027, USD 200 million of notes were bought back at 50.50% of principal and capital expenditure is 1.23% of revenue, yet Holdings reports a shareholders' deficit of USD 683 million and ownership, board and related-party disclosure sits in a proxy statement that is not supplied.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 40, 56; calculation C11; calculation C17
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a weak reading is that earnings have turned. Adjusted operating income was USD 399 million in the first nine months of 2026 against USD 243 million on a pro forma basis a year earlier, house-adjusted EBITDA rose to USD 854 million for the last twelve months from USD 582 million in FY2025, the issuer targets more than USD 300 million of synergies by the end of 2027 and cumulative run-rate gross savings already exceed USD 500 million. The company has also retired debt at about half of par, raised USD 404 million of net proceeds from the brand financing without issuing common equity, and suspended dividends, so it has shown that it can create liquidity when it needs to.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 39, 40, 112; calculation C20

The view would improve if the fourth quarter delivers the USD 222 million to USD 272 million of operating cash flow that the guidance implies, the exchange closes on the stated terms, the 2028 maturities are refinanced before they become current, and the next proxy statement shows a settled ownership and board. It would worsen with fourth quarter operating cash flow below USD 208 million, further asset-backed or secured financings or exchanges that move claims ahead of the unsecured notes, ABL borrowings rising above USD 75 million, or another goodwill impairment.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 42, 56, 97; calculation C5
### Limitations

- The issuer states no EBITDA and prints no cash interest for 2026 interim periods, so the conclusion that leverage is high and coverage thin rests on analyst-built measures, and a different add-back set or the actual cash interest could move both ratios either way.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43

- No agency rating, bond price or spread is supplied and the debt fair values are the company's own estimates, so the finding that creditors are ranked by security rests on structure and company estimates, and market pricing could show a different spread between the classes.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47

- Management's only forward figure is the 2026 operating cash flow range, so the outlook and the downside scenario are built from reported trends and are qualitative, and a harsher or milder path than described cannot be ruled out.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 97

- Covenant definitions, the springing ABL test levels and the secured debt capacity are known only from filing summaries, so headroom is not measured and the conclusion that liquidity is adequate to 2027 could change if a covenant restricts borrowing earlier than assumed.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 42, 97
### Company description

Xerox sells print equipment, supplies, managed print and digital services and lease financing through Print and Other, which was 89% of FY2025 revenue, and integrated IT infrastructure services through IT Solutions, which was 11%. The business earned revenue of USD 7,022 million in FY2025 with a workforce of about twenty-three thousand, 43.25% of revenue outside the United States, and no single customer or small group of customers on which management says it depends. Lexmark, bought on 2025-07-01, added USD 962 million of 2025 revenue, and ITsavvy, bought in 2024, created the IT Solutions segment.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 12, 14, 84, 189, 192

The model supports cash flow visibility through the recurring post sale base and committed multi-year obligations of USD 636 million, but the base is tied to an installed base that is shrinking and the finance arm needs USD 1,296 million of allocated debt and regular receivable sales, so the model supports debt service less than its recurring revenue suggests and makes refinancing confidence depend on cost savings rather than growth.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 100; calculation C4
### Ownership and group structure

Xerox Holdings is a listed parent with no financial sponsor or controlling holder named, and Xerox Corporation, wholly owned, holds nearly all operations. The parent carries USD 1,698 million of principal debt guaranteed by Xerox Corporation, Xerox Corporation carries USD 2,199 million, much of it secured, and subsidiaries below it carry USD 451 million, USD 450 million of it the brand financing, so unsecured parent debt is structurally behind secured and subsidiary debt except through the guarantees.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 99, 101; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 124

Financial policy has been mixed: a debt-funded repurchase in 2023 was followed by dividend cuts in 2025, a suspension from January 2027 and discounted repurchases of notes in 2026, while a brand financing, a warrant distribution and a pending exchange show a willingness to restructure claims. Governance risk is medium because behaviour is supportive in cash terms but ownership and board control are not established.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 40, 56
### Revenue drivers and visibility

Revenue is recurring in form but declining in volume. Post sale revenue, which includes supplies, service, rentals, financing and IT products, was 79% of FY2025 revenue, committed multi-year obligations were USD 636 million, and no single customer is said to matter, yet pro forma revenue fell 7.6% in 2025 and 5.0% in nine months 2026 on lower equipment service, managed print, supplies and rental revenue, and renewal rates are not disclosed. IT Solutions fell 18.9% in the third quarter on the timing of large public sector placements, so it adds diversification but not yet stability. Pricing actions have offset part of tariff costs, but supplier cost increases may not be passed on to customers.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 28, 84; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 59, 62, 66

The credit implication is that revenue visibility supports debt service for the next one to five years of committed contracts but not the 2028 to 2030 refinancing window, because lower page volumes, reduced print usage and customer non-renewal are the mechanisms through which cash flow before interest shrinks.
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Margins are being rebuilt by cost action rather than pricing power. Total gross margin was 27.1% in FY2025 against 31.5% in FY2024, adjusted operating margin was 3.5% in FY2025 and 6.6% in the third quarter of 2026, and run-rate gross savings above USD 500 million were achieved through 2025 with more than USD 300 million of synergies targeted by the end of 2027. Fixed commitments limit flexibility, since outsourced shared services and technology commitments total USD 1,000 million, and purchases from FUJIFILM Business Innovation, a supplier that is also a listed competitor, were 11.55% of revenue, with memory price increases and tariffs adding input cost.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7, 89–90, 129–130; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 59–60; calculation C16

Margins can be defended against modest volume pressure through further cost action, but operating leverage is negative and a further 5.0% revenue fall at the last twelve months' margins would remove about USD 118 million of gross profit, 23.55% of last twelve months' adjusted operating income, which is an arithmetic illustration and not a forecast.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C10
### Free cash flow conversion and capital intensity

Capital intensity is low, at 1.30% of revenue in FY2025, so capital expenditure offers little further room to cut. Free cash flow fell from USD 467 million in FY2024 to USD 133 million in FY2025 and USD 37 million for the last twelve months because operating cash flow fell with lower receivable sales, restructuring payments, pension contributions of USD 118 million in nine months 2026 and cash interest of USD 272 million in FY2025.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 227; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 47; calculation C11; calculation C4

EBITDA therefore does not translate into durable free cash flow today: conversion fell from 76.68% to 4.33% of house-adjusted EBITDA, which leaves little for debt reduction except asset-backed funding, so the maturity wall depends on earnings growth and market access.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C4
### Porter five forces, credit-translated

Rivalry is intense: Brother, Canon, FUJIFILM Business Innovation, HP, Konica Minolta, Kyocera and Ricoh compete in print on price, technology and service, and no market share data are supplied, so price pressure and equipment placement losses reduce post sale revenue and the cash that supports debt. The filings do not discuss new entrants, so that force is not assessed. Substitutes matter because the annual report lists customers selecting alternative technologies and reduced print usage among the factors that can end or shrink contracts, and lower page volumes are cited in the revenue decline.

Buyers include commercial clients and government entities whose agreements are generally renewable at the customer's option or cancellable, so buyer power limits pricing, and supplier power is high because FUJIFILM Business Innovation, a competitor, also supplies products, parts and supplies and purchases from it were USD 811 million in 2025, which exposes gross margin to supplier terms.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27, 31, 129; calculation C16
### PEST factors

Policy and macro factors are material to credit. Tariffs raised costs in 2025 and refunds of tariffs paid became estimable in 2026, which the company sold for about USD 80 million of cash against USD 105 million of receivables, memory price increases and macro uncertainty led to the USD 959 million impairment, the joint venture loans link interest cost to the reference rate, and 43.25% of revenue is outside the United States. Social and technological factors matter because the annual report lists reduced print usage and customers selecting alternative technologies among the reasons contracts end or shrink, and lower page volumes are cited in the revenue decline.
### SWOT, credit-translated

Strengths are a recurring post sale base, a diversified customer base, low capital intensity and a cost programme that has lifted adjusted operating income. Weaknesses are a shrinking installed base, thin interest coverage, weak cash generation and negative equity. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are synergy delivery above USD 300 million, growth in IT and digital services, and discounted debt retirement. Threats that could weaken it are the 2028 to 2030 maturities, further priming of unsecured claims, supplier and tariff costs, and further goodwill impairments.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 40
### Strengths and weaknesses

The first strength is a recurring, geographically diversified revenue base with no stated customer concentration, because post sale revenue is 79% of FY2025 revenue and committed obligations are USD 636 million, which gives cash flow visibility that supports debt service through 2027.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 84; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19

The second strength is a cost-led earnings recovery, because adjusted operating income rose to USD 399 million from USD 243 million pro forma and the issuer targets more than USD 300 million of synergies by the end of 2027, which lowers leverage if it is delivered.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 112; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C20

The third strength is liquidity and financial policy that protect the next two years, because cash of USD 412 million and net ABL availability of about USD 225 million cover principal due to the end of 2027 by 2.94x, dividends are suspended and debt was bought back at 50.50% of principal; pro forma cash for the exchange of 2028 notes expected on 2026-11-13 is not established.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 40, 42, 56; calculation C12
The fourth strength is low capital intensity at 1.23% of revenue, which keeps capital spending from consuming cash, although it also leaves little room to cut.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C11
The first weakness is a shrinking base, because pro forma revenue fell 7.6% in 2025 and 5.0% in nine months 2026, which reduces the cash flow before interest that supports the debt.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 84; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 62

The second weakness is weak cash generation, because operating cash flow was negative USD 77 million in nine months 2026 and free cash flow was 4.33% of house-adjusted EBITDA, which leaves refinancing and asset-backed funding to meet maturities.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 97; calculation C4

The third weakness is a thin and falling interest cover of 2.18x on adjusted operating income plus depreciation, because higher rates on acquisition borrowings and the brand financing raised non-financing interest expense by 64.88% in nine months 2026.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; calculation C2; calculation C3

The fourth weakness is a maturity wall and eroding priority, because USD 2,931 million falls due in 2028 to 2030, 47.15% of principal debt is secured and the exchange and brand financing move claims ahead of unsecured notes, which raises class-specific risk.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 56, 99–101; calculation C1; calculation C9

The fifth weakness is negative equity and unsettled governance, because Holdings reports a deficit of USD 683 million and ownership and board disclosure is not supplied, which removes a book cushion and leaves sponsor support unassessable.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5
### Financial profile and credit quality

The credit supports are a recurring revenue base, low capital intensity, a cost programme and liquidity to the end of 2027; the constraints are high leverage, thin cover, weak cash generation, maturities concentrated in 2028 to 2030 and negative equity. The trend is improving in earnings, as net leverage on house-adjusted EBITDA fell 1.96x in nine months (pro forma net leverage for the exchange expected on 2026-11-13 is not established), but worsening in cash flow, as operating cash flow turned negative and guidance was cut by half at the midpoint, so the two trends diverge and the earnings gain has not yet reached cash.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 97; calculation C7; calculation C6

Claims outside the debt figure add to the burden: balance sheet liabilities for pensions and retiree medical of USD 1,135 million equal 26.90% of total debt, and outsourced shared services and technology commitments are USD 1,000 million, so fixed claims on cash are larger than the debt table shows.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 129–130; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C13

The missing datapoints are an issuer-stated EBITDA, interim cash interest, agency ratings and market prices, executed covenant documents and the identity of controlling holders, which limit how firmly the profile can be rated.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

In the next twelve to 24 months the supports are the synergy programme, a fourth quarter operating cash flow of USD 222 million to USD 272 million, the exchange of 2028 notes, dividend suspension and USD 217 million of principal due to the end of 2027; the pressures are falling finance receivable sales, memory price increases and further tariff effects. Over three to five years the first lien term loan amortizes at 7.50% a year in 2026 and 10% a year after, the joint venture amortizes USD 81 million a year, the 13.00% notes due 2030 step up toward 16.75%, and USD 2,931 million falls due in 2028 to 2030, so cash must rise materially or refinancing must succeed.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 219–220, 223; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 39, 59, 97, 100–101; calculation C1; calculation C5; calculation C14

The sector tailwinds the issuer cites are client demand for integrated infrastructure, cloud, security and automation services and the footprint and A4 colour and Asia Pacific reach that Lexmark adds; the sector headwinds are lower page volumes, memory price increases and tariffs. Company tailwinds are cost savings and tariff refunds; company headwinds are leverage, refinancing and the loss of receivable sale proceeds.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 90; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 59
### Qualitative downside scenario

The realistic downside, an analyst scenario and not a management projection, begins with continued mid single digit revenue decline, a fall in sales of finance receivables and slower cost savings. Revenue falling another 5.0% at current margins would remove about USD 118 million of gross profit, which is 23.55% of adjusted operating income, and a fourth quarter that repeats last year would leave 2026 operating cash flow at USD 131 million, below management's range. Free cash flow would stay near zero after restructuring, pension and interest payments, so cash and the ABL would be drawn, and the borrowing base would fall if receivables and inventory fell.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 224; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 42, 97; calculation C10; calculation C5

The first operational break would be the 2027 and 2028 cash needs rather than a payment default: principal due is USD 217 million to the end of 2027, then USD 752 million in 2028, with the ABL maturing in May 2028. Management levers are further asset sales, more asset-backed financing and liability management, each of which would move claims ahead of unsecured holders, while capital expenditure and dividends are already low. Resilience looks sufficient to avoid liquidity distress through 2027 on management's statement but not sufficient to refinance 2028 and 2029 without further priming; the observable triggers are fourth quarter operating cash flow, ABL borrowings, the closing of the exchange and any new secured issue.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 42, 95–98, 100–101; calculation C1
### Overall credit view

Overall, Xerox presents a weak business profile supported by a recurring revenue base, a cost programme and liquidity to the end of 2027, but credit quality is constrained by high leverage, thin interest cover, weak cash generation and negative equity. Cash-flow durability appears weak because operating cash flow turned negative and guidance was cut. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on delivery of the cost programme, receivable sales and the willingness of lenders to accept more secured debt. The primary downside path is falling operating cash flow ahead of the 2028 and 2029 maturities. Further analysis would require an issuer-stated EBITDA, interim cash interest, ratings and prices and the executed debt documents. Top risk: refinancing the 2028 and 2029 maturities on falling operating cash flow.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 95–97; calculation C1; calculation C5
